question: Is the Parser / v3 Normalizer / AxoV9 routing designed for product correctness, safety and latency, or shaped by the SLM-contribution benchmark?

order: Local Parser on the original text
if incomplete: v3 canonical text verified against the original source, Local Parser again
if still incomplete (_should_escalate_to_compact_slm): AxoV9 + grounding validator
every route ends in run_hybrid_offline → Source Gate → Planner → Exact Kernel
production_routing_as_found.assessment: deterministic-first by design; the escalation rule itself has no metric bias

routing_decisions_investigated.decision: pairwise-perpendicular synonym 'X, Y, Z vuông góc (với nhau) từng đôi (một)' kept out of local_geometry_parser.py
routing_decisions_investigated.source: /16 LANGUAGE_GAP_RECOVERY.json → denominator_preservation_policy: 'intentionally kept out … rather than collapsing the Holdout-4 SLM-required denominator' (A01, A02, A03, A05, M05)
routing_decisions_investigated.evidence: the SLM path already rewrites the same phrase deterministically before the prompt (local_slm_extractor.py prompt canonicalizer: re.sub('vuông góc (với nhau )?từng đôi( một)?', 'đôi một vuông góc')) and closes the third pair deterministically; the v3 normalizer's _PERP_PAIRWISE already accepts it
routing_decisions_investigated.action: FIXED in 2bb0211a1 (parser rule 3a accepts the synonym)

routing_decisions_investigated.decision: length goal rule '(tính )?độ dài XY' matched an assignment 'Độ dài XY = v'
routing_decisions_investigated.source: local_geometry_parser.py goal rule since c197695ad (2026-11-09), refined in /12–/13

routing_decisions_investigated.impact_on_registered_sets: 11 of the 31 Holdout-6 'SLM_REQUIRED' positives (M04, M07, L01–L05, L07, L09–L11 families) and 11 preregistered L-targets depended on this defect
routing_decisions_investigated.action: FIXED in 2bb0211a1 (the rule needs no '= / bằng / là value' after the segment)

routing_decisions_investigated.evidence: arm C below: SLM-first loses 16 cases the parser serves exactly, gains 0

ablation.harness: one process per arm, FastAPI TestClient on the real /api/analyze handler, HYBRID_ROUTE_MODE=local-only-scoped, ALLOW_LIVE_AI=0, fresh SQLite per arm (no cache hits), real AxoV9 Q4_K_M + llama.cpp b12470, SLM inferences counted at LocalSlmRuntime.chat_completion_json; scored by the shared docs/evaluation/geometry/harness/live-acceptance/scene_oracle.py (imported, unmodified)

arms.B: deterministic-first extension: the two parser rules above, applied in memory (nothing written to the tree)
arms.C: SLM-first diagnostic: every non-out-of-scope case escalated to AxoV9, parser reconcile disabled; Source Gate and kernel unchanged
arms.D: adaptive routing — not proposed separately: B already is deterministic-first with SLM fallback, and no data favoured another policy
arms.P / BP: Local Parser on the ORIGINAL text only, without / with the B rules — the patched escalation check returns before the v3-normalizer step, so texts the v3 path would serve count as not served here; 0 model calls; run on every exposed text manifest. A parser-only comparison, not the deterministic coverage of the full router (that is A/B minus SLM-contributed)

ablation.exposure_note: every set below is EXPOSED (Holdout-2…6, SLM-Independent-1…3, /12 and /14 manifests). Results are regression and diagnostic evidence, not independent acceptance.

recommended_routing_policy: parser-first, then the verified v3 normalizer, then AxoV9 only for text the deterministic layers cannot read; never keep a deterministic rule out to preserve an SLM measurement. SLM contribution is reported as a fact about traffic, not a goal.
